Maintenance Report — MNT-0060-002

Asset: WELL-0060 (SW-24 Well 060, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 11 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Mar 2023 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 266 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0060-0021 on 2023-03-09 Report written: 23 Mar 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0060-0021 showed the wellhead at 13.9 °C with the air at 13.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0060-002 (WS-06).

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 16 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0060-023

Asset: WELL-0060 (SW-24 Well 060, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 29 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 15 Apr 2025 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 400 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0060-0126 on 2025-03-27 Report written: 17 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0060-0126 showed the wellhead at 17.5 °C with the air at 16.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.
